title: Stealth Worktree Pipeline
summary: Design for a local-first worktree pipeline that lets the user pre-build work from Linear tickets without triggering Linear status changes. Four new gx verbs (gxstart, gxlist, gxship, extended gxclean) form the lifecycle. gxstart queries the Linear API read-only to generate a branch name and create a worktree. Work stays local and invisible until gxship pushes, creates a PR via gxpush, and lets the GitHub-Linear auto-link handle status transitions. A .worktree-meta.json file in each worktree root tracks ticket identity and state (picked, building, ready, shipped). The find-work skill evolves to wrap gxlist as a shell script. All decisions resolved.
decisions: Work stays local-only during pre-build phase. No pushes to GitHub until ship time.
gxstart accepts a Linear URL or ticket ID, queries the Linear API read-only, generates a branch name, and calls the existing wt engine to create a worktree.
gxstart is a standalone shell script, not MCP-dependent. Works from any terminal.
Linear API authentication uses LINEAR_API_KEY stored in ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env, following the existing secrets pattern used by Notion scripts.
Branch names are auto-prefixed with feat/, fix/, or spike/ based on Linear ticket type. Keeps compatibility with find-work and worktree warnings.
gxship is a wrapper around gxpush. It fetches, rebases onto main, updates worktree meta to shipped, then delegates to gxpush for push and PR creation.
gxship always requires explicit confirmation before shipping. Capital Y is the default (enter = ship).
gxship prompt on building state: 'Ship? [Y/n] -- Ready but later? [r]'. On ready state: 'Ship? [Y/n]'.
gxship displays a descriptive message before the prompt explaining what will happen: rebase onto main, push to GitHub, create PR, trigger Linear to move ticket to In Progress.
No Linear API writes at any point. Read-only at gxstart. Auto-link handles status at ship time.
GitHub-Linear auto-link handles the In Progress status transition at ship time. No explicit API calls needed.
Metadata stored in .worktree-meta.json in each worktree root. Added to global gitignore.
Four states: picked (gxstart created it), building (auto-detected via local commits ahead of base), ready (marked via gxship 'r' option), shipped (gxship completed).
picked to building transition is auto-detected by checking local commits ahead of base branch. No manual step needed.
ready state is set via the 'r' option in the gxship prompt, not a separate gxmark command. Removes a command to remember.
The inventory command is named gxlist. Current repo by default, --all flag for cross-repo view.
gxlist output is grouped by state (READY, BUILDING, PICKED) and includes clickable Linear URLs for each item.
find-work skill evolves to wrap gxlist shell script. Same pattern as worktree skill wrapping the wt engine.
gxclean extended with --full flag to clean worktrees for merged/deleted branches and stale remote branches, in addition to current local merged branch cleanup.
Manual ship timing only. No scheduling or automation. User runs gxship when they decide.
gxstart requires being cd'd into the target repo. Same pattern as wt.
gxship auto-rebases onto latest main (or policy base branch) before pushing. Stops on conflicts.
next_action: Run /to-tasks to generate the implementation task breakdown for the four gx verbs and find-work evolution.
problem_statement: Copying a branch name from Linear's UI triggers a workspace automation that moves the ticket to In Progress and adds it to the current cycle. This creates visible activity trail (status thrashing) when the user pre-builds work and then moves tickets back. The team can see this activity, undermining the goal of trickling out deliveries at a consistent pace.
solution: A four-verb local-first pipeline: gxstart (intake from Linear API without UI interaction), gxlist (inventory dashboard), gxship (push + PR when ready), and extended gxclean (cleanup). Work stays completely local and invisible until explicitly shipped. Metadata in .worktree-meta.json tracks state per worktree.
evidence: Linear activity log screenshot showing repeated 'moved to In Progress, then back to Backlog' entries visible to the entire team within minutes of each other.
implementation_decisions: gxstart lives at ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxstart alongside other gx verbs.
gxstart sources LINEAR_API_KEY from ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env using the same conditional source pattern as the Notion scripts.
gxstart uses a curl call to Linear's GraphQL endpoint to fetch ticket title, type, and project key. No SDK needed.
Branch name format: <prefix>/KEY-NUMBER-slug, matching the existing Linear-generated convention observed in the codebase (e.g. feat/KEY-1234-migrate-experiences).
.worktree-meta.json schema includes: linear_ticket_id, linear_url, ticket_title, branch_name, status, picked_at timestamp.
gxlist scans ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/ and reads .worktree-meta.json from each worktree. Auto-detects building state via git log checking local commits ahead of base.
gxship wraps gxpush. Sequence: read meta, fetch origin, rebase onto base, update meta status, call gxpush.
gxclean --full adds two passes: scan worktrees for merged branches and offer wt rm, then optionally prune remote branches via git push origin --delete.

out_of_scope.text: Linear API writes (status changes, ticket assignment, cycle management)
out_of_scope.rationale: Stealth is the core requirement. Any Linear write creates visible activity. Auto-link at ship time is sufficient.

out_of_scope.text: Automated ship scheduling or delivery queuing
out_of_scope.rationale: User wants manual control over ship timing. Automation adds complexity for minimal gain.
Requires being cd'd into target repo, same pattern as wt. Rare case doesn't justify the complexity.
Decided on standalone shell script with API token. MCP only available inside Claude sessions, which is too constraining.

risks_and_tradeoffs: Local-only work has no remote backup. If the machine dies, pre-built work is lost. Acceptable risk per user decision.
Pre-built branches may accumulate merge conflicts with main over time. gxship's auto-rebase catches this at ship time, but late conflicts could require rework.
The LINEAR_API_KEY is a personal token with read access. If the user's Linear permissions change, gxstart breaks silently.

user_stories.feature: pick up a Linear ticket and create a local worktree without triggering any Linear status change
user_stories.benefit: I can pre-build work invisibly and ship it later on my own schedule

user_stories.feature: see a grouped inventory of all my local pre-built worktrees with their state and clickable Linear links
user_stories.benefit: I can quickly find what's ready to ship and navigate to the ticket for context

user_stories.feature: ship pre-built work with a single command that rebases, pushes, and creates a PR
user_stories.benefit: shipping is fast and the Linear status transition happens naturally via auto-link

user_stories.feature: mark work as ready without shipping it immediately
user_stories.benefit: I can distinguish finished-but-unshipped work from work still in progress

user_stories.feature: clean up merged worktrees, local branches, and remote branches in one command
user_stories.benefit: I don't accumulate stale worktrees and branches across repos

further_notes: The existing find-work skill (Haiku model, lists spike/feat/fix branches) is replaced by gxlist. The skill becomes a thin wrapper.
The gx verb family after this work: gxcheck, gxclean (extended), gxlist (new), gxmove, gxpush, gxship (new), gxstart (new), gxsync.
